sense: turn your body round, as a command

evidence: Plin. Ep. 4.11.9 (Lewis & Short s.v. vertō): vertit sē et recollēgit, she turned round and gathered up her robe
Traupman 34: turn around, tē verte (pl. vōs vertite)
Ov. Met. 7.189 (Lewis & Short s.v. convertō): ter sē convertit

phrases.source: Plaut. Ps. 1.3.29 (Lewis & Short’s numbering), in Leo’s text

phrases.latin: Verte tē, ut tibi tergum lavem.
phrases.english: Turn around so I can wash your back.

sources: Lewis & Short: verto · Lewis & Short: converto
Plautus checked against Leo’s text (1895) at Gadsden Classics, which prints vorte where Lewis & Short has verte.
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
